newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco Cosumar H1 profit up at $19.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco Cosumar H1 profit up at $19.6 mln.

text.p: Morocco's leading sugar company Cosumar showed on Friday provisional profits of 171.1 million dirhams ($19.6 million) in the first half of the year, more than triple those of the same period in 1995.
Cosumar, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, made 48.2 million dirhams in the first half of 1995.
The 1996 half-year profits were mainly due to government subsidies, the firm said.
Cosumar's turnover dropped slightly to 1.68 billion dirhams from January to June 1996 from 1.77 billion dirhams in the first half of 1995.
One of the 46 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, the Compagnie Sucriere Marocaine et de Raffinage (Cosumar) was last traded at 669 dirhams.
Morocco domestic sugar output is estimated at 500,000 tonnes annually. The country is 65 percent self-sufficient in sugar but imports large quantities to satisfy its growing demand.
It imported 477,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1995 at a cost of 1.3 billion dirhams.
Established in Casablanca in 1932, Cosumar has a production capacity of 600,000 tonnes per year.
Since liberalisation of the commodity market earlier this year, Cosumar became the main raw sugar importer instead of the state-owned Office National du The et du Sucre (ONTS), officials said.
